summary.tldr: Prioritizes certain pension and group insurance claims in insolvency proceedings and requires annual reporting on pension plan solvency.
what_it_does: Gives priority in bankruptcy to amounts owed to cover pension plan unfunded liabilities or solvency deficiencies, including required special payments.
Gives priority under the Companies’ Creditors Arrangement Act to similar pension claims when restructuring proceedings begin.
Gives priority to claims tied to an employer ending participation in a group insurance plan in bankruptcy and restructuring cases.
Requires the Superintendent of Financial Institutions to report each year on pension plan funding, the Act’s operation, and corrective steps for plans that do not meet funding rules.
Requires the Minister to table that report in each House of Parliament and sends it to provincial finance ministers and securities commissions.
Delays the new bankruptcy rules for four years for employers and companies already taking part in prescribed pension plans.
summary.background: Amends the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act, the Companies’ Creditors Arrangement Act, and the Pension Benefits Standards Act, 1985.
